pairs.subject: read-serving-replicas
pairs.evidence: apps/desktop/client/src/lib/data/bus.ts:88 An invalidation during a fetch schedules another read after the old answer enters the cache, allowing a stale fill instead of fencing and discarding it.

techniques.evidence: apps/desktop/client/src/lib/data/query.ts:49 Cache misses invoke the single backend directly; searches found no lagging storage replica against which a carried position would be checked.

apps/desktop/client/src/lib/data/bus.ts:118 A failed invalidation subscription only logs an error; cached reads remain enabled without the live channel required by the standard, and no checkpoint or recovery gates their use.

apps/desktop/client/src/lib/data/bus.ts:85 The trailing-read mechanism waits for the in-flight fetch to settle and apply its answer before invalidating again; it has neither an epoch fence nor a lock preventing the stale fill.

apps/desktop/client/src/lib/data/bus.ts:70 This dispatcher scans one window's local query cache; it does not send invalidations through peer or tenant transport queues where a slow recipient could block others.

apps/desktop/client/src/lib/data/invoke.ts:72 Reads execute through the authoritative backend rather than first running handlers against a replica store, so no refused local storage mutation needs forwarding.

apps/desktop/client/src/lib/data/invoke.ts:2 Mutations already bypass the query cache and invoke the backend directly; searches found no response wrapping, one-time consumption, or replica-local dispatch requiring preemptive forwarding.

pairs.registryProposal: Clarify which requirements apply to client-side invalidation/refetch caches: the golden path explicitly includes these copies, while several techniques assume a replica-local storage backend.
